title: How to Prepare Your Sammamish Home for Hardwood Floor Refinishing: The Complete Checklist
meta: Preparing a Sammamish home for hardwood floor refinishing: what to move, where the pets go, thermostat and a day-by-day checklist from Wills Flooring.
keywords: how to prepare for hardwood floor refinishing, what to do before floor refinishing, hardwood refinishing checklist, prepare house for floor sanding, hardwood floor refinishing Sammamish WA

blocks.lead: To prepare a Sammamish home for refinishing, empty the rooms completely, including closets and wall art, plan where the dog and the family will be for three to five days, set the thermostat to normal and leave us a clear path from the driveway to the floor.
blocks.detail: That covers 90 percent of what goes wrong. The rest is timing: booking the painter, the movers and the cleaners in the right order so nobody walks on wet finish. Use the day-by-day checklist below.

blocks.html: A Sammamish refinish is rarely a single room. It is the whole open-plan main floor of a Klahanie or Trossachs two-story, 1,000 to 1,600 sq ft of builder oak that connects the kitchen, dining area and family room with no doors between them. That means everything on that level has to go somewhere, and everyone who lives there, including the dog, needs a plan. Homeowners who prepare well get a faster job and a better finish. Homeowners who do not lose a day to furniture moving and end up with paw prints in the sealer. Here is the schedule we hand our own customers.

blocks.text: Two weeks out: decisions and bookings

items.text: If you are staining, we sample two or three colors on your actual floor at the estimate. Decide now, because stain adds a day and changes the schedule. Most Sammamish floors going lighter need a full sand, not a recoat.
items.note: Natural $3.99, stain $6.50 per sq ft, 500 sq ft minimum.

items.text: Painters do walls and ceilings before us and baseboards after. Cabinet installs and plumbing happen before. Cleaners come after the 72-hour cure, not the day the finish is applied.
items.note: Wrong order is the most common cause of a marred new floor.

items.text: Dogs cannot be on the floor from the first sanding day until the finish has cured to the touch, usually 24 hours after the last coat. Big Sammamish households often send the dog to a relative and the kids to grandparents for the coat days.
items.note: Bona water-based finish has low odor, but wet finish and claws do not mix.

items.text: The three-car garage most plateau homes have is the natural staging area. Clear a bay now. If the garage is full, a portable storage pod for one week is cheaper than paying a crew to move a piano twice.
items.note: Tell us about pianos, aquariums and safes at the estimate.

blocks.text: The week before: clear the floor, not just the furniture

items.title: Furniture, rugs and rug pads
items.text: Everything sitting on the floor leaves the room, including rugs and the rubber pads under them. Rug pads that have bonded to old finish leave a ghost we sand out, but tell us so we plan the time.

items.title: Walls, shelves and closets
items.text: Sanders vibrate. Take down mirrors, pictures and anything on floating shelves. Empty closet floors and the lower shelf of pantries; closets are refinished too and the doors usually come off.

items.title: Electronics and cords
items.text: Unplug and remove TVs, consoles and speakers from the room. Sanding dust is minimal with our vacuum-connected machines, but a fine film still finds unprotected electronics. Remove cords from the floor entirely.

items.title: Appliances
items.text: Fridge, range and dishwasher move if the hardwood runs under them, which it does in most Sammamish kitchens. We move them for $80 each, or a washer and dryer pair for $160. Empty the fridge to the garage fridge and shut off the ice-maker line the night before.

blocks.text: The night before and the morning of

head: Item
What to do
Why it matters
rows: Thermostat
Set to 65 to 75°F and leave it there for the whole job.
Finish cures by evaporation. A cold house doubles dry time.
HVAC
Replace the furnace filter now and again after the job. We tape supply registers on the floor.
Keeps fine dust out of the ducts and off the wet finish.
Windows and blinds
Leave blinds up or removed, windows unlocked for us.
Light shows imperfections during sanding; we ventilate between coats.
Water and power
Confirm the outlets work and note the panel location.
Our big sander runs on 220V; we bring adapters but need panel access.
Driveway and HOA
Clear space for a trailer near the entry; warn the HOA if street parking is limited.
Sammamish HOAs sometimes restrict trailers overnight. A note avoids a tow.
Doors and alarms
Leave a key or code, disable motion sensors on the work level.
We arrive early and leave late on coat days.
Pets
Out of the house before we arrive on day one.
Even a friendly dog in a sanding zone is a hazard for everyone.

blocks.text: Prep mistakes that cost Sammamish homeowners a day

items.html: Stacking furniture in the room next door and blocking the path. The sander and the finish cart need a clear route to every room being refinished. Stage in the garage, not the hallway.
Painting baseboards before the floor. Sanding always scuffs base. Paint it after, or ask us to sand carefully and plan a touch-up.
Letting the dog back in after the first coat. Finish that is dry to the touch is not cured. Claw marks in the sealer mean an extra screen and coat.
Watering plants or mopping the day before. A damp floor reads high on the meter and the stain goes on unevenly. Leave the floor dry and dusty; we clean it.

Booking the cleaners and the movers for the last coat day. Socks after 24 hours, furniture after 72, rugs after two to three weeks. See when you can walk on refinished floors before scheduling anyone.

blocks.title: Open-plan means all or nothing:
blocks.text: On a Sammamish main floor with no doorways between kitchen, dining and family room, there is no natural place to stop. Refinishing half of a continuous floor leaves a visible line. Budget and clear the whole level, or plan the stopping point at a doorway with us before the job starts.

items.html: Two weeks out: stain and sheen chosen, painter and cleaner sequenced, pet plan made, garage bay cleared.
One week out: rugs, pads, wall art, electronics, closet floors and small furniture out. Storage pod delivered if needed.
Night before: fridge emptied, ice-maker off, thermostat set, filter changed, blinds up, driveway clear, HOA notified.
Morning of: pets gone, key or code left, alarm off, one contact phone number on the counter.
After: socks at 24 hours, furniture with felt pads at 72, rugs after two to three weeks. Full details on our refinishing service page.

faq.q: Do I have to remove everything from the room before floor refinishing?
faq.a: Yes. Every item touching the floor comes out, including rugs, rug pads, plants and cords, and closets are emptied because they are sanded too. Wall art and mirrors should come down because the sanders vibrate. Appliances sitting on hardwood are moved; we do that for $80 each.

faq.q: Can I stay in my house while the floors are refinished?
faq.a: On a single room, yes. On a whole Sammamish main floor, most families leave for the two or three coat days because the kitchen and every path through the house are off limits. Sanding days are fine to be home if you can live upstairs.

faq.q: Where should pets go during hardwood floor refinishing?
faq.a: Out of the house from the first sanding day until the last coat has dried at least 24 hours. Bona water-based finish is low odor, but wet finish and claws or fur ruin a coat. A relative's house or a boarding kennel for three to five days is the usual answer.

faq.q: Should I paint before or after refinishing hardwood floors?
faq.a: Walls and ceilings before, baseboards after. Sanding scuffs baseboards and the finish coat can spatter, so painting trim last gives the cleanest result. Wait until the 72-hour cure before painters set ladders on the new floor.

faq.q: What temperature should the house be during floor refinishing?
faq.a: Between 65 and 75 degrees, held steady from the day before sanding until a few days after the last coat. Water-based finish cures by evaporation, so a cold house slows dry times and a very warm, dry house can make the finish set too fast.

faq.q: How much does refinishing cost for a typical Sammamish main floor?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rates a 1,200 sq ft main floor is 1,200 × $3.99 = $4,788 for a natural finish or 1,200 × $6.50 = $7,800 with stain. Add $80 per appliance moved and $250 if you want full dust containment.
